# Model-based Interactive Semantic Parsing: A Unified Framework and A Text-to-SQL Case Study

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#misp)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/D19-1547.pdf) · EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019 proceedings; arXiv:1910.05389v1 Appendices A-C

**Reading coverage:** Proceedings pp. 5447-5458, Sections 1-6, Tables 1-5 and figure captions; arXiv supplementary pp. 13-14, Appendices A-C and Tables 6-12. Rendered Table 5 inspected.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Author manuscript, Appendices A–C](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05389v1#page=13)

## Research question

Interactive semantic parsing needs reusable components for deciding when to seek user help and incorporating that feedback during generation.

## Method

Maintains a partial parse, flags uncertain components using probability or Monte Carlo dropout, asks template-based yes/no questions, and bans rejected alternatives in the base parser. Candidate attempts are capped; rejecting every alternative restores the original prediction.

## Evaluation

SQLNet and SQLova on WikiSQL and SyntaxSQLNet on Spider; ground-truth-driven simulation plus three graduate evaluators per sampled example. The study reports query matching, execution accuracy and question counts; its human sample is 100 examples per base parser.

## What the results support

Selective interaction improves simulated accuracy with fewer questions than exhaustive querying. Human gains are smaller; SQLova execution accuracy is 0.880 versus 0.890 without interaction, despite a slight exact-match gain. Showing table content and gold SQL raises its result to 0.937.

## Limits and qualifications

Human feedback depends on understanding benchmark intent. The full-information condition exposes gold SQL and is not ordinary deployment. Error correction is bounded by the parser’s candidate set and earlier decisions; no request-unanswerability guarantee is provided.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Foundational architecture and evidence that simulator gains and oracle-informed users can overstate practical clarification benefits.
